# cmux NEXT documentation

> Every cmux NEXT guide page in full. In a cmux terminal, `cmux docs guide --full` prints this file, `cmux --help` and `cmux skill show` describe the CLI, and `cmux docs search` searches its commands.

---

# Getting started with cmux-next

What cmux-next is, how to install it, and how to update it.

cmux-next is the rewrite of cmux: a Swift app shell, a Rust core, and web views for chat, diffs, Markdown, and Settings. It runs your terminals, browsers, and coding agents in one window, with Chief on the Home screen.

> cmux-next is in preview. It changes every day. This page is built from the main branch, so it may be ahead of the build you run.

## Install

Two builds exist. Pick one.

- cmux NEXT DEV runs beside classic cmux. It updates after each green push to feat-cmux-next.
- nightly-next takes the place of classic cmux NIGHTLY (same bundle id and socket). It updates through Sparkle about every 30 to 60 minutes. Apple Silicon only.

## Install cmux NEXT DEV

```bash
curl -fsSL -o /tmp/update-dev-daily.sh \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/feat-cmux-next/scripts/cmux-next/update-dev-daily.sh
bash /tmp/update-dev-daily.sh
```

The script downloads the build, checks its SHA-256 and bundle id, and installs ~/Applications/cmux NEXT DEV.app. Run the same command to update. If you have the newest build, it says so and does nothing.

## Install nightly-next

```bash
gh release download nightly-next -R manaflow-ai/cmux -p '*macos-arm64*.dmg'
```

Open the DMG and drag the app to Applications. The app updates itself from then on.

## Coming from classic cmux

The first launch brings over the last saved classic session once: workspaces, groups, panes, tabs, and Claude Code or Codex chats. Classic's files are only read. To run it again, use the command palette item Import Workspaces from Classic cmux, or run:

```bash
cmux workspace import-classic
```

## First steps

- Press Cmd+Shift+P for the command palette. Every action in the app is there, with its shortcut.
- Open Home and ask Chief for what you want in plain words.
- Press Cmd+, for Settings. Every setting is also a key in ~/.config/cmux/cmux-next.json.
- Run cmux --help in a cmux terminal. The CLI can do everything the palette can.

# How cmux NEXT fits together

The app, the daemons that run your terminals and agents, your machines, and cmux Cloud: what each part does and where its code is.

cmux-next is several programs that work together. The window is one of them. Your terminals and agents run in two daemons that keep going when the window closes, on this Mac or on other machines. cmux Cloud, the service behind your account, links the machines.

This Mac runs the cmux app and two daemons: cmux-tui for terminals and layout, and acpmux for agent sessions. Machines you add and Cloud machines run the same two daemons, and acpmux links them. cmux Cloud holds your account, your machines, your vault, and the team hub, and starts Cloud machines.

## The app

The macOS app is a native window around web views and a Rust core. The web views draw the agent chat, diffs, Markdown, and Settings. The Rust core is linked into the app and holds the action catalog, the palette ranking, and the layout rules. Every command in the palette, the menus, the CLI, and the MCP tools comes from that one catalog, so they always match. The iPhone app is another client of the same machines.

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| [`Packages/macOS/CmuxNext`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/Packages/macOS/CmuxNext) | The macOS app, one Swift module per feature |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-app-ffi`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-app-ffi) | The Rust library linked into the app |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-action-catalog`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-action-catalog) | The action catalog: every command, its shortcut and surfaces |
| [`cmux-next-ios`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-next-ios) | The iPhone app |

## Web views

Chat, diffs, Markdown, Settings, Home, and the other pages are React, built from one source tree. The app serves each page from its own cmux-page:// origin, and the page talks to the app only over a small bridge. A dev server can feed them to a running app with hot reload.

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| [`webviews`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/webviews) | The React source and its dev server |
| [`webviews/src/pages`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/webviews/src/pages) | Pages the app hosts: Settings, Home, history, and more |

## Terminals: the cmux-tui daemon

Terminals, panes, and the workspace layout live in the cmux-tui daemon, not in the window. The app keeps a read-only copy and sends the daemon requests over a local socket. So terminals keep running while the app restarts or updates. The cmux CLI and cmux mcp serve talk to the same daemon, which is why they can do everything the app can.

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui) | The cmux command and the cmux-tui daemon |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli) | The CLI, including cmux mcp serve |
| [`cmux-tui/docs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/docs) | cmux-tui docs: concepts, protocol, remote, machines |

## Agents: acpmux

Every agent chat is a session in acpmux, a daemon on each machine. acpmux starts the agent program (a harness: Claude Code, Codex, or one you add), keeps it running by name, records every message, and lets any number of clients attach: the chat in the app, the CLI, or another agent. It also keeps the cost ledger of every turn.

The acpmux daemons on your machines link up. A session on another machine is addressed as MACHINE/NAME. A message to a session can also go through your team's hub in cmux Cloud, which delivers it wherever that session runs.

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/acpmux`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/acpmux) | The agent daemon and its CLI |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/harnesses`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/harnesses) | The harness profiles cmux ships |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/docs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/docs) | acpmux docs: daemon, sessions, harnesses, machines |

## Machines

A machine is any computer that runs cmux-tui and acpmux: this Mac, a computer you add, or a Cloud machine. The sidebar shows each machine's workspaces under its name. Agents on another machine keep running when your laptop sleeps.

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/cli/host_enroll.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/cli/host_enroll.rs) | Add Machine over SSH: reach, install, start, link |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/machine_join.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/machine_join.rs) | cmux machine add: join with a pasted line |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-remote`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-remote) | The remote daemon, its clients and connection |

## cmux Cloud

cmux Cloud is the service behind your cmux account. It starts, pauses, forks, and snapshots Cloud machines, keeps the list of machines you added, holds your vault, runs the team hub, and connects GitHub. A Cloud machine boots from an image that already has cmux-tui, acpmux, and the agents installed. A Cloud chat can start on your paused spare machine, which wakes as you start, so you do not wait for a new one.

A repository describes the machine it needs in .cmux/machine.toml: environment variables, the names of the secrets it needs, setup commands, and checks. cmux applies the file on the machine.

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-cloud-api`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-cloud-api) | The Cloud API client |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-cloud-start-core`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-cloud-start-core) | How a Cloud chat starts, spares included |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-cloud-start-core/src/machine_config.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-cloud-start-core/src/machine_config.rs) | The .cmux/machine.toml format |
| [`web/services/vms`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/web/services/vms) | Cloud machine drivers |
| [`web/services/vms/images/devbox`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/web/services/vms/images/devbox) | The Cloud machine image |

## Secrets and the vault

Keys never go on a command line. A key for an agent you added stays in this Mac's Keychain. A secret a Cloud machine needs stays in the Keychain too, and goes to the machine only over its own connection. Your vault in cmux Cloud gives machines you add their keys, and agents on them get a placeholder: the machine puts the real value only into requests to the hosts you allow.

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-vault-egress`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-vault-egress) | The proxy that puts a vault value into allowed requests |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/machine_join/vault.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/machine_join/vault.rs) | cmux machine vault |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/cloud_secret.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/cloud_secret.rs) | cmux cloud secret |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/cli/harness_secret.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/cli/harness_secret.rs) | cmux harness secret |

## GitHub

Agents use GitHub with your own gh sign-in on this Mac. Connect GitHub to your cmux account for Cloud machines. A machine you added can borrow this Mac's GitHub access for a short list of actions: read a repository or pull request, open a draft pull request, and file or comment on an issue. It cannot push or merge. Agents can ask which GitHub account is connected, but never get a token from it.

```bash
cmux accounts github-connect
cmux cloud setup-github
```

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/github_status.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/github_status.rs) | Which GitHub account an agent can use, never a token |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/github_broker.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/github_broker.rs) | The GitHub actions a machine you added may borrow |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-host/src/github_cli.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-host/src/github_cli.rs) | cmux github: credentials and gh for agents |

## MCP and connectors

cmux is an MCP server: cmux mcp serve gives Claude Code, Codex, or any MCP client the same control of cmux that the CLI has. Agent chats inside cmux have it already.

Connecting other MCP servers to your agents is being built. You will ask an agent to connect a service, approve a card that says what it gets, and sign in in a cmux browser tab. Agents will get the tools, never the token. It is not on in builds yet; this page will link its guide when it is.

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/mcp`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/mcp) | The MCP server (cmux mcp serve) |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-mcp-connect`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-mcp-connect) | Rules for connecting other MCP servers (in progress) |

## Updates

nightly-next updates itself from the update feed; cmux NEXT DEV updates with its script. Quitting to update keeps your sessions: the daemons keep your terminals and agents running, and the new app attaches to them. A daemon still on the old version shows Restart Recommended in Settings > Server, and restarts only when you choose.

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| [`Packages/macOS/CmuxUpdater`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/Packages/macOS/CmuxUpdater) | The app updater and its channels |

# Install, update, and nightly

How cmux-next updates and how to check your build.

## Updates

- nightly-next: the app checks the update feed and shows a Restart to Update card. Restart relaunches at once. Your terminals, agents, and chats come back.
- cmux NEXT DEV: run the update script again.

Quitting keeps sessions by default. Agents keep running in the acpmux daemon while the app restarts.

## Check your build

```bash
cmux version
```

## Server restarts

When the app and the background server are on different versions, Settings > Server shows Restart Recommended. cmux never restarts the server on its own. You choose when.

---

# Home and Chief

The Home screen, Chief, and group chats.

Home is the first screen. It looks like a messages app. Each row is a conversation: a Chief, a person on your team, or a group chat.

Chief is your assistant. You ask in plain words. Chief starts agents, opens panes, and reports back in the same thread.

## Commands

```bash
cmux home open-chief      # open Chief
cmux home tab             # open Home in a tab
cmux home new-chief       # make another Chief
cmux home send            # send a message
```

## Teammates

People in your team show up as contacts. You can message one, or start a group chat with several people and Chiefs.

In a group chat, use Hide Alerts to mute, Pin/Unpin Conversation to keep it on top, and Leave Group to leave.

---

# Agents and subagents

Run Claude Code, Codex, and other agents as chats.

An agent runs as a chat tab. The chat shows messages, tool calls, and diffs. The agent itself lives in acpmux, a daemon, so it keeps running when the app closes.

## Start and stop

```bash
cmux agent quick          # start an agent
cmux agent new-chat       # new agent chat in this pane
cmux agent stop-turn      # stop the current turn
cmux agent archive-chat
```

## Fork a conversation

A fork copies the conversation so you can try another path. Fork to the right, left, above, below, a new column on either side, a new row, a new tab, a new workspace, or a new window.

```bash
cmux agent fork-conversation-to-right
cmux agent fork-conversation-to-new-column-right
cmux agent fork-conversation-to-new-workspace
```

## Teams

```bash
cmux agent launch-claude-teams
cmux agent launch-codex-teams
```

## Subagents

A subagent is an agent another agent started. It gets its own workspace and chat, so you can open it, read it, and stop it like any other.

- [acpmux, the agent daemon](acpmux.md)
- [Run agents on your own API keys](own-keys.md)
- [Open-weight models](open-models.md)
- [Audit agent spend](agent-spend.md)

# acpmux, the agent daemon

How cmux keeps agents running: sessions, harnesses, machines, and the daemon.

acpmux keeps coding agents running as named sessions. One acpmux daemon runs on each machine. cmux starts it; the app's chats, the cmux CLI, and other agents are all clients of it. When the app quits or updates, your agents keep working.

## Sessions

A session is one agent conversation. It has a name of up to 80 letters, digits, dots, dashes, and underscores. A session on another machine is MACHINE/NAME. acpmux records every message a session sends and receives, on disk, so any client can attach later and read the whole conversation.

cmux acp gives you acpmux from the cmux CLI:

```bash
cmux acp ls                                       # sessions on every machine
cmux acp new -n fix-tests -m codex -d "Fix the failing test"
cmux acp send fix-tests "Also run the linter"
cmux acp wait fix-tests --print                   # wait for the turn, print the reply
cmux acp last fix-tests                           # the last reply
```

## Harnesses

A harness is the agent program a session runs: Claude Code, Codex, and other agents. acpmux talks to agents with the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), and through adapters to agents that speak their own protocol. Each harness is a profile in ~/.config/cmux/harnesses/ that says how to start it.

```bash
cmux acp daemon harnesses   # the harnesses this daemon knows
cmux acp daemon models      # the models each one offers
cmux harness add gateway --example anthropic-endpoint --base-url https://llm.example.com --model MODEL
```

## Machines

The acpmux daemons on your machines link up, over SSH or your private network. Then a session on any of them shows in your sidebar, and you can start one where you like. A message to a session can also go through your team's hub in cmux Cloud: it is delivered at least once and runs once, wherever that session runs.

```bash
cmux acp machine ls         # your machines and their connection state
cmux acp machine status     # health: reachable, disk, load, sessions, build
cmux acp machine pick       # which machine a new session would go to, and why
```

## The daemon

```bash
cmux acp daemon status
cmux acp daemon restart     # sessions resume after
cmux acp daemon shutdown    # agents keep running for the next daemon
```

The daemon also keeps the cost ledger: when a turn ends, it adds the turn's cost and tokens. Read it with cmux acp ledger.

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/acpmux`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/acpmux) | The agent daemon and its CLI |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/docs/cli-sessions.md`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/docs/cli-sessions.md) | Every session command |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/docs/cli-harnesses.md`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/docs/cli-harnesses.md) | Harness profiles and how to add one |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/docs/cli-hosts.md`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/docs/cli-hosts.md) | Machine commands |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/harnesses`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/harnesses) | The harness profiles cmux ships |

# Run agents on your own API keys

Use your own API key, your cloud provider, or your own model endpoint for Claude Code, Codex, and other agents in cmux.

Yes: cmux runs Claude Code, Codex, and other agents on your own API keys, and the key's own account is billed. cmux does not meter these agents or see their bill.

## How do I use my own API key with Claude Code in cmux?

cmux reads your key the way Claude Code does, so a key that works in your terminal works in cmux. Pick one of three ways.

- From your shell. Export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in ~/.zprofile or ~/.zshrc. The agent daemon reads your login shell, so every Claude Code chat gets the ANTHROPIC_* and CLAUDE_* variables your terminal has. A change to those files applies to the next chat you start. An apiKeyHelper in Claude Code's settings.json works too.
- From a chat. When Claude Code is not signed in, the chat's sign-in card has Use an API key. cmux saves the key where Claude Code reads it (env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in Claude Code's settings.json) and starts the chat again on it.
- For one chat. In the model picker, choose Add account…, then Use an API key. Give where the key is, not the key: keychain:NAME, env:VARIABLE, or file:/absolute/path. Then pick that account in any chat. Other chats keep their own account.

```bash
# ~/.zprofile
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your-key
```

## How do I use Claude through my cloud provider?

Turn on Claude Code's own provider switch in your login shell. cmux passes it to every Claude Code chat. It passes the provider's credential and region variables too, but only when your own switch is on.

```bash
# ~/.zprofile: one of these, with the provider's usual variables
export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1   # AWS_REGION, AWS_PROFILE, ...
export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1    # CLOUD_ML_REGION, ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID, ...
export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1
```

Claude Code's own setup for each provider works as it does in a terminal. cmux only passes the variables through.

## How do I use Codex with an API key?

Codex keeps its API key in its own login. When Codex is not signed in, the chat's sign-in card has Use an API key: cmux runs codex login --with-api-key and gives it the key on stdin, so the key is never on a command line. In a terminal, the same step is:

```bash
printenv OPENAI_API_KEY | codex login --with-api-key
```

OPENAI_* and CODEX_* variables in your login shell reach Codex chats too.

## How do I connect my own model endpoint?

An endpoint that speaks Claude's Messages API, or the Chat Completions API (OpenAI-compatible), becomes an agent with one command. It can be a company gateway, a team inference server, or a model server on this Mac.

```bash
# Messages API, run through Claude Code
cmux harness add gateway --example anthropic-endpoint --base-url https://llm.example.com --model MODEL
cmux harness secret set gateway ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
cmux harness doctor gateway

# Chat Completions API (compatible endpoint), run through OpenCode
cmux harness add local --example openai-endpoint --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 --model MODEL
cmux harness secret set local CMUX_BYO_API_KEY
cmux harness doctor local
```

- secret set asks for the key without showing it, or reads it from stdin. It keeps the key in the Keychain on macOS (secret-tool on Linux). The agent's profile file holds only the item's name.
- The base URL must use https. Plain http works only to localhost, 127.0.0.1, or ::1.
- doctor sends one real prompt. When it fails, it says what to fix: the key, the base URL, or the model id.
- The new agent shows in the model picker. Your own Claude sign-in and ANTHROPIC_* variables never redirect it.
- A compatible endpoint runs through OpenCode, so install OpenCode first.

## How do I give an agent on a Cloud machine my key?

- Claude Code and Codex: when a Cloud chat is not signed in, its sign-in card offers to sign in to Claude or Codex, or Use an API key. Either one signs in that machine only. Your Mac's login stays on your Mac.
- Other keys a repository's machine needs: list their names under [secrets] in the repository's .cmux/machine.toml, then store each value on your Mac with cmux cloud secret set. The value stays in your Mac's Keychain and goes to the machine only over its own connection. Names that would send agents elsewhere (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL, and others) are refused there.

```bash
cmux cloud secret set MY_SERVICE_KEY
```

On machines you add yourself, your vault can keep a key out of the agent's reach. Agents get a placeholder (cmux-secret://NAME), and the machine adds the real value only to requests to the hosts you list:

```bash
cmux machine vault set MY_SERVICE_KEY --host api.example.com
cmux machine vault grant MACHINE
```

## Does cmux keep prompt caching on with my own key?

Yes. cmux never turns prompt caching off, and it starts every Claude Code chat on the one-hour cache. By itself, Claude Code uses the five-minute cache with an API key, your own endpoint, or a cloud provider: after a pause of more than five minutes, the whole prompt is written again. With the one-hour cache, a chat you come back to within the hour reads its prompt from the cache.

Writes to the one-hour cache cost a little more than writes to the five-minute one. To use five minutes:

```bash
cmux settings set agents.promptCache 5m
```

The setting applies to chats you start after the change. A cache variable you set yourself (CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL, FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M, DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING) wins over it.

- [Audit agent spend](agent-spend.md)
- [Open-weight models](open-models.md)
- [Plans and credits](plans.md)
- [Cloud machines](cloud.md)

---

# Audit agent spend

See what every agent turn on this Mac cost, by session, workspace, repository, pull request, day, person, provider, or model.

The Costs tab in Agent History shows what every agent on this Mac spent, whichever agent ran it, grouped the way you choose.

## Where do I see what my agents cost?

Open the command palette, run Show Agent History, and pick the Costs tab. It reads the cost ledger of this Mac's agent daemon, which adds up each turn when the turn ends. So the tab opens at once, however many chats you have.

## What does the Costs tab show?

- A range: 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, or all time.
- Totals for the range: cost, tokens in, tokens out, turns, tool calls, and agent time.
- One row per group, most spent first, with a bar for its share: cost, tokens in and out, turns, and agent time.
- Tokens in counts uncached input and cache writes. Cache reads are the same context sent again, so they are not counted.

## How do I group agent spend by repository, pull request, or person?

Pick a group: session, workspace, repository, pull request, day, person, provider, or model. cmux adds a session's pull requests as they open, so a pull request's row adds up every session that worked on it. Person is the user and machine that ran the agent.

## Where does each cost come from?

Each cost is marked with its source:

- Reported by the agent: the agent's own figure for the turn.
- Priced from the table: the turn's tokens at the price table that ships with cmux. The tab shows the table's version.
- Partly priced: a group whose turns had different sources, such as some reported and some from the table, or some with no price.
- No price known: no turn had a price, because the table does not list the model.

A turn with no price adds nothing to the cost. When the tab counts turns with no price, the cost shown for that range or group is incomplete: the real cost is at least that much.

A table price is an estimate at list prices, not a bill. On a subscription, the figure is what the same tokens would cost on the API, not what you pay. A fork's copy of its parent's turns counts once, in the parent.

## Can I read agent spend from the command line?

```bash
cmux acp ledger                              # the last 7 days, by repository
cmux acp ledger --since 30d --by pr          # the last 30 days, by pull request
cmux acp ledger --since 1d --by model --json # today, by model, as JSON
```

--by takes repo, pr, day, person, workspace, vendor, model, or account. --since takes a length such as 30m, 6h, or 7d.

## What does it cover?

Every turn that ran on this Mac's agent daemon, with any agent: Claude Code, Codex, or one you added. Each machine keeps its own ledger. Run cmux acp ledger on a machine to read that machine's.

- [Run agents on your own API keys](own-keys.md)
- [Plans and credits](plans.md)
- [Agents and subagents](agents.md)

# Open-weight models

Run coding agents in cmux on open-weight models: on this Mac, on your own GPU machine, or on a server your team runs.

Point an agent at any server that speaks the Chat Completions API (OpenAI-compatible), on this Mac, on your own GPU machine, or on your team's inference server, and it runs in cmux like Claude Code or Codex.

## Which agents in cmux can run open-weight models?

Any agent whose models come from providers you set up. cmux knows OpenCode and Pi out of the box: install one and it shows in the model picker, using the providers you set up for it in your terminal. Add any other agent that speaks ACP in Settings > Agents, or with:

```bash
cmux agent add-harness
```

The simplest path is your own endpoint, below: one command makes the agent, and cmux keeps its key in the Keychain.

## How do I run an agent on a model server on my Mac?

Start the model server, then add it as an agent. Local servers usually listen on localhost and serve the Chat Completions API under /v1.

```bash
cmux harness add local --example openai-endpoint --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 --model MODEL
cmux harness secret set local CMUX_BYO_API_KEY
cmux harness doctor local
```

- MODEL is the id the server lists for the model.
- A server that takes no key still needs a value stored. Any text works.
- This agent runs through OpenCode, so install OpenCode first.
- doctor sends one real prompt. A first prompt can wait while the server loads the model. doctor waits up to 120 seconds per step; --timeout gives it longer.

## How do I use a model server on my own GPU machine?

Two ways. Neither puts the server on the public internet.

Agent on your Mac, model on the GPU machine: forward the server's port over SSH, then add the forwarded address as above. A server with its own https address works directly with that address.

```bash
ssh -N -L 8080:127.0.0.1:8080 gpu-box
```

Agent and model both on the GPU machine: add the machine to cmux (Add Machine… in the command palette, or the command below). Then, on that machine, add the endpoint at its own localhost.

```bash
cmux acp machine enroll gpu-box

# then, on gpu-box:
acpmux harness add local --example openai-endpoint --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 --model MODEL
acpmux harness secret set local CMUX_BYO_API_KEY
acpmux harness doctor local
```

On Linux, harness secret set stores the key with secret-tool, so the machine needs a running secret service. Then start a chat on that machine (cmux remote new-workspace) and pick local in the model picker.

## How do I use my team's inference server?

Add it with its https address and the key your team gives you. cmux refuses plain http to anything but localhost, so a server without https needs a forwarded port, as above.

```bash
cmux harness add team --example openai-endpoint --base-url https://llm.example.com/v1 --model MODEL
cmux harness secret set team CMUX_BYO_API_KEY
cmux harness doctor team
```

## Can a Cloud machine run an open-weight model?

Not yet: Cloud machines have no GPU today. Run the model on your own machine or on a server your team runs. cmux inference also serves open-weight models, paid with cmux credits.

- [Run agents on your own API keys](own-keys.md)
- [Remote machines and Tailscale](remote.md)
- [Plans and credits](plans.md)

# Workspaces, panes, tabs, and groups

How cmux-next lays out your work.

A window holds workspaces. A workspace holds panes. A pane holds tabs: terminals, browsers, chats, files, and more.

## Panes

```bash
cmux pane split-right
cmux pane split-down
cmux pane equalize-splits
cmux pane move-to-new-workspace
```

## Tabs

```bash
cmux tab new-terminal
cmux tab new-browser
cmux tab rename
cmux tab move-to-pane-left
```

## Workspace groups

Groups gather related workspaces in the sidebar. A group has a name, color, and icon. It can hold subgroups, and you can pin, collapse, or mark it read.

```bash
cmux workspace-group create
cmux workspace-group add-workspace
cmux workspace-group set-color
cmux workspace-group collapse-all
```

## Hibernation

A workspace you have not opened for a while hibernates: its pages and chats are unloaded to free memory. Terminals and agents keep running. Pinned workspaces, workspaces with running commands or agents, and workspaces you keep awake never hibernate. Change it with workspaces.hibernation.enabled and workspaces.hibernation.idleMinutes.

- [Spaces and columns](spaces.md)
- [Command palette](command-palette.md)

---

# Spaces and columns

Group windows and workspaces into spaces, and dock columns to the window.

A space is a named set of windows and workspaces, for example Work and Personal. Each space has its own color, icon, theme, terminal defaults, and groups. The sidebar shows your spaces at the top or bottom (sidebar.showSpaces, sidebar.spacesPosition).

## Switch spaces

Use Next Space, Previous Space, or Select Space 1…9. The default keys are on the Keyboard shortcuts page. From the CLI:

```bash
cmux space switch
cmux space new-workspace
cmux space new-window
```

## Change a space

```bash
cmux space rename
cmux space set-color
cmux space set-icon
cmux space set-theme
cmux space set-defaults
cmux space move-left
cmux space delete
```

Set Space Terminal Defaults gives new terminals in the space their folder, shell, and environment. Set Space Theme changes the colors of every window in the space.

## Columns

A column is a strip of panes. Dock a column to the left, right, top, or bottom of the window: it stays there when you switch workspaces. Float it to put it over the window, or undock it to put it back in the workspace.

```bash
cmux column dock-left
cmux column dock-bottom
cmux column float
cmux column undock
cmux column width-half
cmux column center
```

- [Workspaces, panes, tabs, and groups](workspaces.md)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](keyboard-shortcuts.md)

# Command palette

Every command in the palette, with its default shortcut and CLI command.

Press Cmd+Shift+P to open the command palette. Type a few letters of a command, then press Return. The palette also finds workspaces, tabs, files, and settings.

Start the query with a scope prefix to search one kind of thing. Set the prefixes in Settings > General (the palette.scopes keys).

```bash
cmux palette open
```

This list is generated from the action catalog, the same catalog the app builds its palette, menus, CLI, and MCP tools from. A test fails when the catalog changes and this page does not.

The full table is generated from the app's own catalog. In a cmux terminal, `cmux action list` print it.

# Browser

Browser tabs, profiles, and automation.

Browser tabs open inside a pane. A tab can use Chromium or WebKit.

```bash
cmux tab new-browser
cmux browser open-in-chromium
cmux browser open-in-webkit
cmux browser screenshot-page
cmux browser import-cookies
```

## Profiles

Browser profiles keep cookies and sign-ins apart. Manage them with the cmux browser-profile commands.

## Automation

Agents drive browser tabs through the cmux CLI and MCP tools. See the CLI and MCP reference for the full list of browser verbs.

---

# Markdown and files

View and edit Markdown and other files in a pane.

Markdown files open as rendered pages in a pane. Click a link in a terminal to open the file in the right viewer.

```bash
cmux file open
```

Other file types open in the editor or the file preview. Use Open Files as Pane to browse a folder beside your terminal.

# Cloud machines

Run workspaces on cloud machines.

A cloud machine is a remote computer that cmux sets up for you. Run a workspace there, or move one over and bring it back.

```bash
cmux cloud new-machine
cmux cloud new-workspace
cmux cloud ssh
cmux cloud exec
cmux cloud move
cmux cloud bring-back
```

## Terminals

Open a terminal on a machine with ssh, or make a new workspace there. Pass --workspace with a workspace id to add a terminal tab to that workspace instead. When the terminal is open, both answer machine_id and workspace_id, plus the new terminal's surface_id when cmux knows it. A paused machine resumes first: if that takes longer than about 30 seconds the answer is pending (machine_id, resuming, pending) and the terminal still opens.

```bash
cmux cloud ssh --target machine:<id>
cmux cloud new-terminal-on-machine --target machine:<id>
cmux cloud new-terminal-on-machine --target machine:<id> --workspace <workspace-id>
```

## Start an agent on a machine

Start a Claude or Codex session on a cloud machine. Name the machine with --target, or give a name with --name to use that machine or create it. An agent that runs this asks you first in its chat.

```bash
cmux cloud start-session --target machine:<id> --agent claude
cmux cloud start-session --name dev --agent codex
```

## Fork, snapshot, hand off

```bash
cmux cloud fork-machine
cmux cloud snapshot-machine
cmux cloud restore-machine
cmux cloud hand-off-machine
```

## Ports and browser tabs

Open a port of a machine in a cmux browser tab, or get its link. Name the machine with --target machine:<id>; cmux cloud list-machines lists the ids.

```bash
cmux cloud open-browser --target machine:<id> --port 3000
cmux cloud machine-link --target machine:<id> --port 3000
cmux cloud port-forward --target machine:<id> --port 3000
cmux cloud port-list --target machine:<id>
cmux cloud port-close --target machine:<id> --port 3000
```

> Running machines do not update themselves. New software reaches new machines first.

- [Machines](machines.md)
- [Remote machines and Tailscale](remote.md)
- [Secrets and the vault](vault.md)
- [Plans and credits](plans.md)

# Secrets and the vault

Where cmux keeps API keys and other secrets, and how agents use a key without seeing it.

cmux never takes a secret on the command line. Each command below asks for the value without showing it, or reads it from stdin, and lists only names afterwards. Which one to use depends on where the agent runs.

## A key for an agent you added

An agent you added with cmux harness add keeps its key in the Keychain on macOS (secret-tool on Linux). Its profile holds only the item's name.

```bash
cmux harness secret set gateway ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
```

## Secrets for Cloud machines

A repository lists the secrets its machine needs under [secrets] in .cmux/machine.toml. Store each value on your Mac. It stays in your Mac's Keychain and goes to the machine only over its own connection. Pass --repo OWNER/NAME to keep a value for one repository.

```bash
cmux cloud secret set DATABASE_URL
cmux cloud secret set DATABASE_URL --repo acme/api
cmux cloud secret ls
```

## The vault, for machines you add

Your vault keeps keys in your cmux account for the machines you add. A machine gets it when it joins with cmux machine add --vault, or when you grant it later. Each key says how agents get it:

- --host H: agents see a placeholder, cmux-secret://NAME. The machine puts the real value in only when a request header carries the placeholder to a host you listed. Other hosts, the URL, and the body never see it.
- --no-hosts: agents get a placeholder that is never replaced.
- --env: agents get the real value in their environment. This is weaker: an agent can read it.

```bash
cmux machine vault set MY_SERVICE_KEY --host api.example.com
cmux machine vault ls
cmux machine vault grant MACHINE
cmux machine vault revoke MACHINE
```

The vault never holds a Claude or Codex sign-in. Sign in on each machine through the agent's own flow.

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/cli/harness_secret.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/cli/harness_secret.rs) | cmux harness secret |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/cloud_secret.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/cloud_secret.rs) | cmux cloud secret |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/machine_join/vault.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/machine_join/vault.rs) | cmux machine vault |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-vault-egress`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-vault-egress) | The proxy that puts a vault value into allowed requests |

# Machines

This Mac, computers you add, and Cloud machines: what runs on each, and how they join.

A machine is a computer that runs your terminals and agents. Each one runs the same two daemons: cmux-tui for terminals and workspaces, and acpmux for agent sessions. The sidebar shows each machine's workspaces under its name.

- This Mac. cmux starts its daemons when you open the app.
- A computer you own: a Mac mini, a Linux box, or a server. cmux installs its daemons for you.
- A Cloud machine: a computer cmux Cloud runs for you. It starts with the daemons and agents installed.

## Add a computer you own

Over SSH: run Add Machine… in the command palette and give its host name. The Remote machines page has the steps.

Without SSH: cmux machine add prints one line to paste on the other computer. The line holds a single-use token that expires after 10 minutes. The computer joins your cmux account and shows in your sidebar.

```bash
cmux machine add                  # print the line to paste
cmux machine add --vault          # the same, and give the machine your vault
cmux device list                  # every device that can reach yours
cmux device doctor NAME           # check an SSH machine step by step; --fix repairs
cmux device revoke NAME           # remove a machine that joined with a pasted line
```

## Cloud machines

cmux Cloud starts, pauses, forks, and snapshots Cloud machines. A Cloud chat can start on your paused spare machine, which wakes as you start, so you do not wait for a new one.

A repository describes the machine it needs in .cmux/machine.toml. cmux applies it on the machine: it writes the environment, reports any named secret not delivered yet, runs setup in the checkout, and reports the checks. Setup runs again only when the file changes. Secret values never reach setup or checks.

```toml
version = 1
[env]
NODE_ENV = "development"
[secrets]
names = ["DATABASE_URL"]     # names only; values come from cmux cloud secret set
[setup]
run = ["bun install"]
timeout_minutes = 30
check = ["bun run typecheck"]
```

## Which machine runs a new session

You pick the machine when you start a chat. With --machine auto, acpmux picks the least-loaded machine you allow; pick says which one and why.

```bash
cmux acp machine pick
cmux acp new --machine auto -m codex -d "Fix the flaky test"
```

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/machine_join.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/machine_join.rs) | cmux machine add: join with a pasted line |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/machine_doctor.rs`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/cli/machine_doctor.rs) | cmux machine doctor |
| [`cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/devices`](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/tree/feat-cmux-next/cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui/src/devices) | cmux device: every device that can reach yours |

# Remote machines and Tailscale

Run workspaces and agents on your own machines over SSH or Tailscale.

A remote machine is a computer you own: a Mac mini, a Linux box, or a server. cmux installs cmux-tui on it, starts its agent daemon, and shows its workspaces in your sidebar under the machine's name. Agents on it keep running when your laptop sleeps.

## Add a machine

Open the command palette and run Add Machine…, or click + in the Machines part of the sidebar. Type a host name, or pick a device from your Tailscale network. cmux then:

- checks that it can reach the host with SSH keys (no passwords);
- installs cmux-tui on the host;
- copies your agent profiles across and starts the agent daemon;
- shows a checklist. Run it again at any time with Check Machine.

```bash
cmux machine add
cmux machine doctor
cmux remote connect
```

## Tailscale

When Tailscale runs on this Mac, Add Machine lists the online devices of your tailnet, and marks the ones that are already added. Only your own devices are probed. A teammate's machine shows only when they share it with you.

Connections go over SSH on your tailnet. cmux opens no public port.

## Work on a machine

```bash
cmux remote new-workspace
cmux remote open-terminal-here
cmux remote reconnect
cmux remote disconnect
cmux remote forget
```

Browser tabs in a remote workspace can open the machine's localhost ports (browser.remoteLocalhost).

## When it does not connect

- Run Check Machine. Each failed step says what to fix.
- Make sure ssh HOST works in a terminal without a password.
- Run Copy SSH Error from the command palette to get the full message.

- [Cloud machines](cloud.md)

# Plans and credits

What is free, what costs money, and how cmux credits work.

> Paid plans for cmux-next are in preview and not on sale yet. Prices and limits can change before launch. This page says how billing works, not what it costs.

## Free

- The app, the CLI, terminals, browser tabs, remote machines, and Home are free.
- Agents that use your own Claude Code or Codex sign-in, or your own API key, are free. cmux does not meter them or see their bill.

## cmux credits

cmux credits pay for what cmux runs for you: models through cmux inference, and cloud machine time. One credit is one US dollar. Buy credits in the app; they work with or without a plan.

When an agent's model needs a key you do not have, the chat shows a card with three choices: add your own API key, use cmux credits, or add credits.

## Plans

A paid plan adds included credits each month, more cloud machines at once, and larger machines. Team plans pool the included credits of all seats. Use above the included amount is charged at cost or taken from prepaid credits.

## See your usage

Open the command palette and run Chief Usage, or Upgrade to cmux Pro to see the plans. Your accounts and sign-ins are in Accounts:

```bash
cmux accounts show
```

- [Cloud machines](cloud.md)
- [Run agents on your own API keys](own-keys.md)
- [Audit agent spend](agent-spend.md)

# CLI and MCP reference

Every cmux CLI command and which are also MCP tools.

Every action in the app can run from the CLI. This page is generated from the action catalog. It cannot drift: a test fails when the catalog changes and this page does not.

```bash
cmux <noun> <verb>
cmux action list
cmux action run <id>
```

A verb marked no under MCP tool is CLI only, because it needs credentials, ends the app, changes the system, or only moves focus.

The full table is generated from the app's own catalog. In a cmux terminal, `cmux --help`, `cmux <scope> --help` and `cmux action list` print it.

- [MCP server](mcp.md)

# MCP server

Give Claude Code, Codex, or any MCP client control of cmux.

cmux mcp serve gives an MCP client the same control of cmux that the CLI has. It talks JSON-RPC on stdin and stdout; nothing listens on the network. Agent chats inside cmux have it already.

## Turn it on

For clients outside cmux, the server is off until you turn it on:

```bash
cmux settings set mcp.enabled true
cmux mcp tools
```

## Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add cmux -- cmux mcp serve
```

## Codex

```toml
# ~/.codex/config.toml
[mcp_servers.cmux]
command = "cmux"
args = ["mcp", "serve"]
```

When cmux is not on the client's PATH, use the one in the app: /Applications/cmux.app/Contents/Resources/bin/cmux.

## Tools

By default the server offers two tools: cmux_docs searches every cmux tool, and cmux_exec runs a short script that calls them. This keeps the client's tool list small. With --all-tools it offers every tool directly:

- one tool per app action, named app_ and the CLI words (cmux workspace rename is app_workspace_rename). The CLI and MCP reference lists each name;
- tools for workspaces, panes, tabs, terminals, and git (workspace_list, terminal_input_write, git_status);
- browser tools (browser_navigate, browser_repl_eval) and agent tools (agents_snapshot, agents_wait).

```bash
cmux mcp serve --all-tools
cmux mcp tools --json
```

cmux mcp tools --json lists every tool with its input schema, and every action it leaves out with the reason. A tool never steals focus unless its purpose is focus.

- [CLI and MCP reference](cli.md)

---

# Settings reference

Every setting, its key, and its default.

Open Settings with Cmd+, or edit ~/.config/cmux/cmux-next.json. The key below is the path in that file: dots go one level down.

```json
{
  "history": { "commandRetentionDays": 30 }
}
```

This page is generated from the settings schema, so it matches the app.

The full table is generated from the app's own catalog. In a cmux terminal, `cmux settings get` print it.
